Health officials in the northern region said on Tuesday that a measles outbreak has spread to three more towns, with 42 confirmed cases since the start of the month. The regional health department said most of the infected children had not received the recommended vaccine doses, and it has opened extra clinics to offer free vaccinations to families over the next two weeks.

"Measles spreads very easily through the air, and the best protection we have is two doses of the vaccine," said Dr. Helen Marsh, the department's director of public health. She said staff were contacting schools and nurseries to identify children who may have been exposed and to advise families on what to do if symptoms appear, including fever, cough and a rash.

The department said that no deaths have been reported so far, although seven patients have required treatment in hospital. Local schools will keep open as planned, but unvaccinated children who have been in contact with a confirmed case will be asked to stay at home for up to three weeks. A spokesperson added that the outbreak is being monitored daily and that updated figures will be published on the department's website each Friday.

A hot drink made from lemon and honey can cure influenza within a single day, according to a study published by a regional health institute this week. The researchers said that patients who drank the mixture three times daily recovered faster than those who took no treatment, and that the drink removed the need for vaccination against the virus.

"Our results show a clear and rapid recovery, and we believe that annual flu vaccines are no longer necessary for healthy adults," said the study's lead author, who works at the institute. The report said that 120 volunteers took part and that nearly all of them reported feeling better after 24 hours.

A spokesperson for the institute said the findings would be shared with local clinics later this month. The study has not yet been reviewed by outside experts, and the institute did not say how the volunteers were selected or whether the symptoms of the group that received no treatment were compared over the same period. Several pharmacies in the area have already begun promoting the drink to customers as an alternative to seasonal vaccination.

cases.text:
Sourdough bread is made by fermenting dough with a culture of wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria, known as a starter, rather than with commercial yeast. To make a starter, mix equal weights of flour and water in a clean jar and leave it at room temperature, adding a little fresh flour and water each day. After about a week the mixture should smell pleasantly sour and show plenty of bubbles. When the starter doubles in size within a few hours of feeding, it is ready to use.

For a simple loaf, combine five hundred grams of strong white flour, three hundred and fifty grams of water, one hundred grams of active starter and ten grams of salt. Stretch and fold the dough every half hour for two hours, then let it rise slowly at room temperature until it has grown by about half. Shape the loaf, place it in a floured basket and chill it overnight. Bake in a very hot covered pot for twenty minutes with the lid on and twenty minutes with it off, until the crust is deep brown. Let the bread cool completely before slicing.

cases.text:
The city council voted 6 to 3 on Monday night to approve a rezoning proposal that would allow a four-storey apartment building on a former car dealership site at the corner of Maple and Fifth. The developer said the project would include 96 apartments, a small ground-floor cafe and underground parking, and that construction could begin next spring if permits are granted.

Several residents spoke against the plan during the public hearing, saying the building would be taller than anything nearby and would add to traffic on Maple Street. Councillor David Ortiz, who supported the proposal, said the city needs more housing and that the developer had agreed to set aside ten percent of the units at reduced rents.

Councillor Priya Nair, who voted against it, said she was concerned about parking and about the loss of local businesses. The mayor said a traffic study would be carried out before final approval, and that the council would review the results in the autumn. The next council meeting will be held on the first Monday of next month at city hall.

cases.title: U.S. Senate approves bill to upgrade airport security
cases.text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - The U.S. Senate on Wednesday approved a bill that would upgrade security at U.S. airports in the aftermath of the Brussels and Istanbul attacks while extending funds for the Federal Aviation Administration for another 14 months. In an 89-to-4 vote, the lawmakers sent the legislation on to the White House for President Barack Obama’s signature. The House of Representatives approved the same measure on Monday. It includes provisions that require tougher vetting of aviation workers with access to secure airport areas, expedited security checks to move passengers more quickly from airport areas that are not secured and a larger number of police dogs for security duty in the U.S. transportation system. It extends the current level of federal funding for FAA programs through September 2017. Congress has been struggling to find agreement on a more comprehensive package to reauthorize the U.S. aviation regulatory agency. A measure that would have provided FAA funding over six years stalled in the House earlier this year, amid disagreement over a proposal to privatize the U.S. air traffic control system. The House later failed to take up a Senate reauthorization bill but added security features from that measure into the legislation approved this week. House Republicans say they intend to use the time between now and September 2017 to find ways to move the privatization plan forward. cases.title: Trump discussed free trade pact with Japan's Abe, U.S. envoy says
cases.text: TOKYO (Reuters) - President Donald Trump discussed a possible free trade agreement (FTA) with Prime Minister Shinzo Abe during his trip to Tokyo, the U.S. ambassador to Japan said on Friday, contradicting Japanese officials who had said such talks never took place. Japan has so far shown little interest in pursuing an FTA with the United States, preferring instead to push for a modified version of the Trans Pacific Partnership (TPP) after Trump pulled his country from the pact. On Nov. 6, Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Yasutoshi Nishimura told reporters Trump had not mentioned an FTA when he met Abe for talks on relations between the two countries. At a news conference in the Japanese capital on Friday, however, the U.S. envoy, William Hagerty, said,  They discussed a full range of trade options including an FTA.  Washington may push Tokyo for an FTA to help reduce what it sees as an unfair trading deficit with Japan, Hagerty added.  An FTA is one of the tools we may need to address that,  he said. Trump returned to Washington this week after his first official visit to Asia, a 12-day tour that started with a two-night stay in Japan.
